title: What the run record is actually for
target: How to use the record R.E.P.O. keeps of a run, given that the game stores the team, the time played, the upgrades and every purchase.
version: R.E.P.O. v0.4.0, as installed for this build (see the sources page for the exact version string)
prerequisites: Access to the shop between runs
A crew that agrees what the record is for

steps.do: Name the team before the first run, because the save keeps the name.
steps.because: the save stores a team name and the player names (teamName)

steps.do: Check the purchase total when you want to know where the money went.
steps.because: items bought and a running total are both kept (itemsPurchasedTotal)

steps.do: Match the upgrade names on the record against what the crew actually has.
steps.because: the game carries a name for every upgrade it knows about (localizedUpgradeSpeed)

steps.do: Use the time played to judge whether a run is still worth continuing.
steps.because: the game tracks how long has been played (timePlayed)

steps.do: Read the result screen at the end rather than trusting memory.
steps.because: the game keeps a result screen of its own (ResultScreenUI)

commonMistakes: Never naming the team and then wondering which save is which.
Ignoring the purchase total until the money is already gone.
Assuming the record carries between runs without checking.
sources: This installation of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
